name: John Markus Lervik
current_role: Founder, Cognite (Oslo industrial data/AI software); CEO until April 2022, then Chief Strategy & Development Officer
profile: Norwegian tech entrepreneur (b. 1969) with an NTNU PhD. He was CEO of Fast Search & Transfer until Microsoft bought it in 2008, founded ad/analytics firm Cxense in 2010, and in 2016 co-founded Cognite, the Aker-backed industrial DataOps company described as Norway's first unicorn. Girish Rishi took over as CEO in 2022; Cognite now lists Lervik as Founder.
interesting_fact: When he handed over the CEO role in 2022, Cognite's announcement credited him with building Cognite into 'Norway's first unicorn'.
deep_cut_fact: He was the first person hired at Fast Search & Transfer, and he won an Esso academic award for his NTNU PhD work in 1996. He is a fellow of the Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences.

public_contacts.value: michelle.holford@cognite.com (Michelle Holford, Global PR Lead, Cognite)

notes: Strong fit for the energy/data angle: Cognite does industrial data for oil and gas and utilities. Avoid the 2014 FAST accounting conviction. Cognite now lists him only as 'Founder', so his day-to-day role may be smaller. The PR email was in the media-contact box on a Cognite newsroom page.

name: Pablo Zamora
current_role: President of the board, Fundación Chile (since 2022, proposed by President Boric). Co-founder and former CSO of NotCo. Investor and board member.
profile: Chilean biochemist with a PhD in biotechnology from Universidad de Santiago. In 2015 he co-founded NotCo, the AI-driven plant-based food company later valued as a unicorn, with Matías Muchnick and Karim Pichara. He was CSO from 2018 to March 2020, then left to work as an investor and consultant. He chairs Fundación Chile, whose board is split between the Chilean state and BHP, and was named to BancoEstado's board.
interesting_fact: Fundación Chile's board, which he chairs, is half appointed by the Chilean state and half by the mining company BHP. That gives him a seat where mining, energy and innovation policy meet.
deep_cut_fact: Before NotCo he did postdoctoral research on the genetics of Mexican maize at UC Davis from 2009. He also worked on plant and microbe genomics as a senior scientist with the Mars Advanced Research Institute (2013-2015).
notes: Spanish-language media covers him often (DF, El Mercurio). A 2026 DF piece hinted his Fundación Chile tenure may end with the change of government; I could not confirm his current status. He has spoken publicly about lithium (the SQM-Codelco deal), which fits an energy podcast. No personal email found.

name: Alexander Kent-Braham
current_role: Co-founder of Marshmallow (London car-insurance insurtech); per 2021 coverage he leads internal culture and product while his twin Oliver handles external matters
profile: British entrepreneur from south-west London who co-founded Marshmallow with his identical twin Oliver and engineer David Goaté. Marshmallow is a licensed UK car insurer that uses data to price cover for people traditional insurers turn away, such as recent migrants and drivers with thin credit files. It became a unicorn in 2021 with an $85M Series B at a $1.25B valuation.
interesting_fact: Marshmallow was only the second UK start-up with Black founders to be valued at more than $1 billion, after WorldRemit.
deep_cut_fact: Marshmallow was first incorporated in 2016 under the name 'Twin Thinking'. For its first 10 months the team worked from the lobby of a Virgin Active gym on an £80 membership ('a desk plus a sauna and a steam room').
notes: His twin Oliver is the usual press voice, so Alexander gives few interviews. I found no published press email for Marshmallow; the gym anecdote is quoted from Oliver in the Evening Standard (syndicated on Yahoo). I could not verify his current title.
